A 10-year-old female patient is hospitalized for a respiratory infection. She resides in foster care and
has a history of multiple hospitalizations. Since birth, she has experienced recurring frontal sinus
pain/pressure and a persistent productive cough. She recently completed a course of amoxicillin for an
infection. Her growth has consistently remained at the 25th percentile for both height and weight since
birth. Her foster parents report normal bowel movements and appropriate weight gain. Her medical
history includes tricuspid stenosis, and a recent chest MRI revealed airway dilation. Current vital signs
show: temperature 98.3°F (37.5°C), blood pressure 102/55 mmHg, pulse 106/min, respirations 13/min,
and oxygen saturation 94% on room air. Physical examination reveals shin bruises attributed to soccer
activities by her guardians. Further examination is incomplete due to the patient becoming tearful.
Which of the following clinical findings is typically associated with this patient's underlying condition?
Answer Choices: (A) Systolic murmur best heard at the apex (B) Diastolic murmur best heard along the
right lower sternal border (C) Clubbing of the fingers and toes (D) Recurrent otitis media with effusion
(E) Failure to thrive with delayed puberty (F) Hyperinflation of the lungs on chest X-ray (G) Positive

antinuclear antibody (ANA) titer (H) Increased chloride in the patient's sweat (I) Social withdrawal and
avoidance of eye contact (J) Decreased serum immunoglobulin levels
 A. Systolic murmur best heard at the apex
B. Social withdrawal and avoidance of eye contact
C. Decreased serum immunoglobulin levels
D. Increased chloride in the patient's sweat
E. Failure to thrive with delayed puberty
F. Diastolic murmur best heard along the right lower sternal border
G. Positive antinuclear antibody (ANA) titer
H. Hyperinflation of the lungs on chest X-ray
I. Clubbing of the fingers and toes
J. Recurrent otitis media with effusion
